## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Restore `>=` in the release approval check before merge: `approved` now rejects a release that has exactly the minimum number of approvals, which contradicts the module docstring. The catalog also gains a non-service `review_note` entry that should be removed.

## Changes
The pull request renames all 1500 entries in `aaa-generated/catalog.json` from `legacy-service-*` to `production-service-*`, moves their ports from 10000–11499 to 20000–21499, and adds a top-level `review_note` key. It also rewrites `healthy` as `not failures` and changes `approved` from `approvals >= minimum` to `approvals > minimum`.

## Critical
- zzz-release/gate.py:5 — correctness — Restore `>=` in the release approval check — `approved(2)` with the default `minimum=2` now returns False, so a release with exactly the required approvals is blocked. The docstring at `zzz-release/gate.py:1` still says "A release needs at least the configured number of approvals", and the existing tests cover only 3 and 1 approvals. — Every release that meets the documented minimum exactly is rejected, and no existing test fails for it. — Fix: Use `approvals >= minimum` and extend `test_approved_release` in `tests/test_release.py` with the `approved(2, minimum=2)` case.

## Important
- aaa-generated/catalog.json:6002 — correctness — Remove the non-service `review_note` entry from the catalog — The added `review_note` key maps to a free-text string, while the other 1500 keys map a service name to an object with `port` and `enabled`; a consumer reading `entry["port"]` for every key raises TypeError on it. No code in this repository reads the catalog, so this review traced no consumer. — Deployment tooling that iterates the catalog as services fails on this key, which carries no deployment data.

## Suggestions
- services/registry.py:88 — silent-failure — `healthy(None)` now reports healthy instead of raising — `healthy(None)` raised TypeError from `len(failures)` before this change and now returns True, so a caller whose failure collection yields None gets a healthy result. — A missing health-check result passes as healthy with no signal to the operator. — Fix: Keep `len(failures) == 0`, or reject None explicitly before `return not failures`.
